answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies runs on a bonded identity registry. Each agent locks a slashable deposit in escrow and passes hardware attestation from a trusted kernel, so one machine cannot mint extra wallets. The registry is a ledger whose stable ledge is the duplicate check: a second claim from the same root is rejected outright. Identity proofs are signed with a per-device cipher, so forging registrations is detectable. Faking N agents forces N frozen deposits through the whole epoch plus failed forgery cost. With slashing, the farm is unprofitable.
